title: /f99b1f8b-e1f2-42cf-9266-3fcd7d56b972/t1
text: can you help help me get a google drive oauth set up or similar so that i can make an app that lets people connect to the gmail but ideally I can't see their content?

title: /f99b1f8b-e1f2-42cf-9266-3fcd7d56b972/t1
text:
Yes. The way to make "I can't see their content" true is architectural: the Gmail calls happen in the user's browser, and your server never holds a token or a message.

## The architecture

**Browser-only OAuth with Google Identity Services (token model).** A static page loads `accounts.google.com/gsi/client`, calls `google.accounts.oauth2.initTokenClient({client_id, scope, callback})`, and gets a short-lived access token directly in the browser. It then calls the Gmail REST API (`gmail.googleapis.com`, which allows CORS) from the page. Any summarizing, indexing or model work also runs in the browser, which fits your local-model approach.

- **No refresh tokens.** The token model gives 1-hour access tokens. Re-requesting with `prompt: ''` renews silently while the user is still signed in to Google and has already consented.
- **Why not auth-code flow?** Google's "Web application" client type requires a client secret at the token exchange, even with PKCE. That means a backend that sees the tokens, which defeats the goal.
- **What you do hold:** the OAuth client ID, which is public, and the static files. You never have credentials, so you can't be compelled or breached into exposing mail.

**If you need to persist anything**, such as an index or settings, use Drive's `drive.appdata` scope. It gives a hidden per-app folder in the user's own Drive and is a non-sensitive scope. Encrypt the data with a key that only the user holds, derived from a passphrase, so even a Drive-side compromise doesn't expose it.

## Gmail scopes need verification

`gmail.readonly` and `gmail.modify` are **restricted** scopes. To go public (past the 100-test-user cap) you need:

- a verified domain
- a privacy policy
- a demo video
- Google's review

My recollection is that apps whose restricted-scope data is processed only on the user's device, and never sent to your servers, are exempt from the paid annual third-party security assessment (CASA). That exemption is the main financial reason to go browser-only. I haven't checked it against the current policy, so confirm it in Google's "Restricted scope verification" docs before relying on it.

In Testing mode you can use up to 100 listed test users with no verification, but their consent expires after 7 days. That's fine for building.

## Honest limits

"Can't see it" means you've built no path to it. It isn't a cryptographic guarantee, because you could still push JS that exfiltrates mail. To make the claim credible, open-source the client, serve it as static files, and say so on the consent-screen privacy policy.

## Setup steps (these need your hands, in your Google account)

1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and create a project.
2. Enable the **Gmail API**, plus the **Drive API** if you want `drive.appdata`.
3. Open Google Auth Platform → Branding/Audience. Choose **External**, add yourself as a test user, and fill in the app name and support email.
4. Open Data Access and add the scopes: `gmail.readonly` (or `gmail.modify`), `drive.appdata`, and `openid email`.
5. Open Clients → Create → **Web application**. Add Authorized JavaScript origins (`http://localhost:8080` and later your real domain). You don't need redirect URIs for the token model.
6. Copy the **client ID**. Don't use or ship the secret.

I won't click through the console or enter credentials for you. Once you have a client ID, I can write a small static page that signs in, lists the last few Gmail threads entirely client-side, and optionally writes a test file to `appDataFolder`. I'd test it on localhost, in this repo or a fresh folder.

Do you want just Gmail read access, or also Drive appdata storage? And should the scaffold go in `3.0/` or a new directory?

5. **Create the client:** go to [Clients → Create](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients/create?project=utility-emitter-433716-k0). Choose **Web application** and add `http://localhost:8080` under **Authorized JavaScript origins**. Leave redirect URIs empty. Click Create, then copy the **client ID**. Ignore the secret.

The page requests only `gmail.readonly`. If you also want the hidden Drive storage folder, add `drive.appdata` as noted in the comment in the file, and in step 4.
